labs.title: Properties of Acids & Bases 3D Lab
labs.description: Test litmus paper, phenolphthalein, methyl orange, and pH strips on common acids and bases in an interactive 3D chemistry bench.
instructions: Inspect the reagent bottles and pH indicator strips on the 3D lab bench.
Test at least two acidic solutions and observe the indicator color changes.
Test at least two basic solutions and compare their pH values.
Record your observations and complete the verification check below.

observationPrompts: What color does blue litmus turn in an acid?
What pH range did you observe for basic solutions?

verificationQuestions.prompt: Which indicator turns pink/magenta in a basic (alkaline) solution?
A solution with pH 2 is classified as:

labs.title: 3D Acid-Base Titration Laboratory
labs.description: Perform a controlled burette titration, add indicator drops, swirl the conical flask, and detect the exact neutralization endpoint.
instructions: Set up the burette and conical flask with the analyte and indicator.
Open the stopcock to add titrant gradually while swirling the flask.
Slow down near the endpoint until a faint persistent color change appears.
Record the final burette reading and verify your titration result.

observationPrompts: What burette volume (mL) was required to reach the endpoint?
How did the indicator color change at neutralization?

verificationQuestions.prompt: Why do we add titrant drop-by-drop near the titration endpoint?
options: To avoid overshooting the exact neutralization volume

verificationQuestions.prompt: At the equivalence point of a strong acid–strong base titration, the pH is:

labs.title: Temporary Mount of Leaf Peel (Stomata) 3D Lab
labs.description: Prepare a temporary leaf peel mount, stain with safranin, focus under the 3D compound microscope, and inspect guard cells and stomata.
instructions: Peel the lower epidermis of the leaf and place it on the glass slide.
Add stain and glycerin, then gently lower the coverslip without air bubbles.
Focus the 3D microscope from low power to high power to view stomata.
Record your observation of the guard cells and complete the check.

observationPrompts: Describe the shape of the guard cells surrounding each stomatal pore.

verificationQuestions.prompt: Which cells control the opening and closing of a stomatal pore?
Why is glycerin used when mounting the stained leaf peel?
options: To prevent the specimen from drying out

labs.title: Human Heart 3D Anatomy & Circulation Lab
labs.description: Rotate, zoom, and inspect the 4 chambers, valves, aorta, and pulmonary vessels of the 3D human heart.
instructions: Rotate and zoom the 3D heart model to inspect both anterior and posterior views.
Select labels for the Right Atrium, Right Ventricle, Left Atrium, and Left Ventricle.
Trace the path of deoxygenated and oxygenated blood through the vessels.
Record your findings and complete the circulation check.

observationPrompts: Which chamber has the thickest muscular wall and why?

verificationQuestions.prompt: Which chamber pumps oxygenated blood into the aorta for the entire body?
Which vessel carries deoxygenated blood from the heart to the lungs?
